narrationTexts: I'll take a look at the log file.
finalText:
# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status at handoff:** ONGOING. Logs end 2026-03-14 03:59:27Z still failing. No rollback recorded.

## Root cause

Deploy **`dep-4471`** (gateway, 02:12–02:14Z, a.novak, *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"*) flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest: false → true` against a **20-connection pool**. Every request now takes its own connection, so the pool exhausts the moment concurrency exceeds 20. The same config bump also raised `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 → 2500`, so each borrowed connection is held longer, compounding it.

Single error type, 530 occurrences, no others in the file:

```
ERROR access req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
ERROR pool   req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

Causal chain is explicit in the log — the pipeline itself requested the reload:

| 02:12:12.820Z | `config reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119` |
| 02:13:41.234Z | `generation 119 applied` — `perRequest: false -> true` |
| 02:14:14.920Z | first `WARN pool ... acquire slow` |
| 02:14:18.972Z | **first 503** (37s after config applied) |

## Impact window

**02:14:18.972Z → 03:59:27.974Z (105 min, ongoing).** Clean before: every request 200, `pool_wait` 0–3ms.

- **530 × 503s**, steady 5/min, no recovery
- Pool pinned `size=20 in_use=20 idle=0` for the entire window; wait queue reached 192
- Latency on failing requests drifted 659ms → 850ms
- All five customer endpoints hit evenly (~106 each): `/v1/cart`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/session`. **Checkout is affected.**
- All four upstreams evenly (132–133 each) — confirms gateway-side, not a downstream service
- Counts are from **node-3 of 3**. If the other two nodes got the same config, multiply by ~3.

## Action

**Roll back `dep-4471`** — revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`. Reverting is safer than raising pool size; sizing the pool above peak concurrency would also work but needs a number nobody has right now.

Verify after: `pool stats` should return to `in_use` well below 20 with `waiting=0`, and `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` should stop.

Deploys `dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41) and `dep-4473` (catalog-svc, 03:20) both landed *after* 503s were already steady and changed neither rate nor signature — **do not roll these back.** Note `dep-4473` starts one minute before the on-call page, which will look like the culprit to anyone scanning backwards from the alert. It isn't.

## Two follow-ups (not blocking the rollback)

**1. `/health` returned 200 on all 180 checks, including through the outage.** Health checks bypass the connection pool, so the node looked healthy to the LB the whole time. On-call wasn't paged until **03:21:05Z** — 67 minutes in — and only then on an error-rate threshold (`error_rate 5m avg is 71%`). Health check needs to exercise the pool.

**2. Unrelated worker regression, still unalerted.** `worker.log` shows **zero failures** — all 1,080 jobs OK, DB pool idle at `in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` throughout. Workers were never involved in this incident. But job latency climbs linearly ~+11ms/min with no ceiling, +2000ms across the window, hitting every job type equally (`reindex` 200→2200ms, `email` 231→2231ms). `db_wait` stays flat at 5ms, so the time is in-process, not the database. It was **already climbing at 01:00Z, the first line of the log and 74 min before the gateway broke**, with no inflection at 02:14 — independent cause, onset is off the left edge of this window. Nearest suspect is `dep-4470` (worker, 00:48–00:55, "retry backoff for webhook jobs"), which finished 5 min before the log starts, but I can't confirm that here — a backoff change shouldn't slow `reindex` and `email` identically. Needs worker logs from before 00:48. On current slope it will breach whatever timeout it meets next.
